overview: West African Resources is an ASX-listed, Perth-headquartered gold miner operating entirely in Burkina Faso, West Africa, through two production centres: the flagship Sanbrado gold mine (producing since March 2020, open pit and underground, ~11-year mine life including the Toega deposit) and the newer Kiaka gold mine (construction completed ahead of schedule and under budget, first gold poured June 2025, transitioned to operations phase 1 August 2025, 18-year mine life). The company is unhedged, sells gold at spot, and is targeting sustained production above 480,000-500,000oz per annum through the early 2030s as it becomes a mid-tier, two-mine West African gold producer.

business_model.summary: Single-commodity gold producer generating revenue entirely from unhedged spot gold sales from two Burkina Faso mines. Revenue is transactional (tied to gold price and ounces sold, not recurring/contracted), with earnings highly leveraged to gold price given a relatively fixed cost base. The business has transitioned from a single-mine (Sanbrado) cash generator funding Kiaka construction capex (FY2023-FY2024 free cash flow negative) to a two-mine cash-generative producer from H2 2025 onward.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - gold sold to refiners/bullion market at prevailing spot price, no customer concentration risk in the traditional sense
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% of production and revenue-generating assets located in Burkina Faso; corporate head office and ASX listing in Perth, Western Australia; gold sold internationally at USD-denominated spot prices, reported in AUD

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-tier West African gold producer; among the lowest-cost operators in the region historically via Sanbrado (site sustaining cost US$1,348/oz in 2025), though Kiaka's AISC during ramp-up (~US$1,702-1,823/oz) is running materially higher than Sanbrado, pulling group AISC guidance to below US$1,900/oz for 2026. WAF has ~A$4.3B market cap (Sept 2026) with an unhedged production profile of 430,000-490,000oz guided for 2026, rising toward a targeted average of 533,000oz/year from 2026-2035.

moat_factors.description: 6.5Moz combined Ore Reserves (2025) across Sanbrado (incl. Toega) and Kiaka provide multi-decade mine life (Kiaka alone 18-20 years) at historically competitive AISC versus global gold industry averages, though Kiaka ramp-up costs currently exceed Sanbrado's.

Established relationships, permits, and operating track record (Sanbrado producing since 2020, zero major disruption) give WAF an established position in the Markoyé fault exploration belt (1,113km2 land package) versus new entrants.

100% unhedged production means full upside exposure to record gold prices (US$4,744/oz realised H1 2026), directly driving record profit and cash flow - a double-edged advantage that is a moat only in a rising gold price environment.
Consistent multi-year track record of growing Ore Reserves (4.6Moz in 2022 to 6.5Moz in 2025) and 10-year production targets through organic exploration, reducing reliance on M&A.

weaknesses: Single-country asset concentration - 100% of production in Burkina Faso, a jurisdiction under military government since a 2022 coup, with an active jihadist insurgency in parts of the country

Rising resource nationalism - Burkina Faso's 2024 Mining Code entitles the state to acquire up to 30% additional paid equity in mining projects (on top of a 15% free-carry), demonstrated by the government's move to take Kiaka SA ownership from 15% to 40% (WAF's stake falling from 85% to 60%)
Kiaka ramp-up costs currently well above design/steady-state economics (AISC ~US$1,700-1,900/oz vs Sanbrado ~US$1,240-1,488/oz), diluting group-level cost leadership during the transition period
No geographic diversification outside Burkina Faso to offset single-jurisdiction political/regulatory risk
Government royalty regime escalates with gold price (7% up to 12%+ as gold price rises above US$3,000/oz), capping some of the upside from record gold prices

growth_drivers: Kiaka ramp-up to full nameplate throughput (~10Mtpa) through 2026, targeting 240,000-280,000oz in 2026 versus 95,155oz in its first five months (partial year) of 2025

Toega gold deposit development - pre-strip mining beginning 2026, first ore deliveries to the Sanbrado plant expected to supplement feed as Sanbrado's own open pit ore depletes; maiden underground reserve targeted for 2027
Sanbrado underground growth (M1 South and M5 South) - M5 South entering stoping production Q4 2026, continued high-grade underground mining supporting Sanbrado's cost profile
10-year production target of average 533,000oz/year (2026-2035), peaking at 596,000oz in 2030, driven by both production centres running concurrently at scale
Ongoing exploration across the 1,113km2 Markoyé fault land package (100,000+ metres of drilling planned in 2026) to extend mine lives and convert resources to reserves
Owner-mining transition (completed at Sanbrado and implemented at Kiaka/Toega in 2025) expected to reduce contractor mining costs over time versus prior outsourced model

Record gold price environment (spot gold exceeding US$4,700/oz in H1 2026 realised terms) directly flowing through to record profit, operating cash flow and a strengthening net cash balance sheet (A$488M net cash at 30 June 2026)

business.description: Kiaka faced an explosives permit issue in Q2 2026 that reduced open-pit mining and required mine plan adjustments to free-dig areas; further permitting or operational delays could affect 2026 guidance delivery
Entire production, cash flow and asset base concentrated in two mines in one country; any single-site disruption (safety incident, equipment failure, grid power loss) has outsized group impact
A contractor fatality at Kiaka in January 2024 and two lost-time injuries in FY2024 highlight ongoing safety risk in open-pit/underground mining operations
Transition from contractor to owner-mining at Sanbrado, Kiaka and Toega in 2025 introduces execution and equipment-reliability risk as WAF operates its own mining fleet for the first time at scale

financial.description: Gold is sold in USD but WAF reports in AUD; costs are incurred in a mix of USD, AUD, CFA franc and other currencies, creating translation and transaction exposure - FX rate moved from 0.6341 to 0.7021 AUD/USD between H1 2025 and H1 2026
Other expenses rose 2,879% in H1 2026 versus H1 2025 mainly due to withholding taxes on higher intercompany dividends declared by Burkina Faso subsidiaries as profits and repatriation increased

financial.risk: Escalating Burkina Faso gold royalty regime
financial.description: Royalty rate is no longer capped at 7%; it now rises stepwise from 7% (at $2,000-3,000/oz) to 12%+ at gold prices above $5,000/oz, directly compressing margin capture from further gold price appreciation

regulatory.risk: Burkina Faso government increasing equity stake in Kiaka SA
regulatory.description: Under the 2024 Mining Code, the government can acquire up to an additional 30% paid equity stake in mining projects on top of its 15% free-carry. The government requested to acquire 35% of Kiaka SA in August 2025 (triggering an ASX trading suspension); this was subsequently formalised via decree (April 2026) at 25% for ~CFA70bn (~A$175M), bringing total Burkina Faso ownership of Kiaka SA to 40% (WAF's stake falling from 85% to 60%). Transaction expected to complete by end of 2026. Sanbrado and Toega ownership are unaffected by these discussions to date, but the precedent raises risk of similar demands at other WAF assets or from other West African governments.

The revised Mining Code and the state vehicle SOPAMIB were created specifically to increase government/resource-sovereignty participation in mining projects; WAF's free-carried government interest across Sanbrado, Kiaka and Toega SA already rose from 10% to 15% in 2025 with priority dividends to the state now non-discretionary at 15% of distributable profits

regulatory.risk: Broader West African resource nationalism trend
regulatory.description: Mali and Burkina Faso have both pursued increased state ownership and renegotiated terms with foreign miners in recent years (echoing precedents at other operators in the region); WAF is not immune to further changes in mining code, taxation, or licence conditions

Operations depend on mining licences and permits (e.g., Sanbrado licence renewed for 5 years in 2024, Toega licence issued 2024) and explosives/operational permits (a 2026 explosives permit issue at Kiaka curtailed open-pit mining), all subject to Burkina Faso government discretion

macro.description: Burkina Faso has been under military government since Captain Ibrahim Traoré's October 2022 appointment as Interim President following a coup. While WAF characterises government leadership as 'stable' and mining/community relations as generally cooperative, the country faces an active jihadist insurgency in parts of its territory, and West African military governments have shown a pattern of renegotiating or expropriating greater shares of mining assets. WAF's shares were suspended from ASX trading in August-November 2025 pending disclosure of a Burkina Faso government stake request - illustrating how quickly sovereign risk can crystallise into a material corporate event.

As an unhedged producer, WAF's revenue, profit and cash flow are fully exposed to gold price swings in both directions; while currently a tailwind (record gold prices above US$4,700/oz), a material gold price correction would sharply compress margins, especially during Kiaka's higher-cost ramp-up phase
Mining and processing operations (including diesel-generated power at Kiaka prior to national grid connection in December 2025) are exposed to fuel, consumables and imported equipment cost inflation
Landlocked Burkina Faso relies on cross-border logistics for equipment, consumables and gold export; regional instability (Sahel security situation) could disrupt supply chains

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Gold mining sector benefiting from a record gold price environment through 2025-2026 (realised prices above US$4,700/oz in H1 2026 versus ~US$2,391/oz in FY2024), driven by central bank buying, geopolitical uncertainty and monetary policy expectations. West African gold belt (Burkina Faso, Mali, Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana, Senegal) remains a globally significant, relatively under-explored gold province attracting continued investment despite elevated sovereign risk.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - gold mining is a cyclical, commodity-price-driven business; WAF's unhedged strategy amplifies both upside and downside cyclicality relative to hedged peers
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity - gold prices are inversely correlated with real interest rates and the US dollar; falling/low real rates have been a tailwind for the current gold bull market benefiting WAF
key_input_costs: Burkina Faso government royalties (now uncapped and price-escalating) and taxes

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 result: record profit after tax of A$436.6M (up 103% YoY), operating cash flow A$689.8M (up 322%), free cash inflow A$344.3M, swinging to a A$488.2M net cash position; declared a 20 cents/share special (unfranked) dividend funded by Kiaka stake sale proceeds, record date 18 September 2026, payment 7 October 2026

Record Q2 2026 quarterly gold production of 125,179oz and operating cash flow of A$249M; Kiaka produced 67,571oz despite an explosives permit issue that curtailed open-pit mining, requiring a shift to free-dig mining areas

Burkina Faso government published a formal decree authorising SOPAMIB to acquire an additional 25% equity interest in Kiaka SA for ~CFA70bn (~A$175M), bringing total government ownership of Kiaka SA to 40% (WAF's interest reducing from 85% to 60%); transaction expected to complete by end of calendar 2026

WAF issued 2026 production guidance of 430,000-490,000oz group gold production (Sanbrado 190,000-210,000oz; Kiaka 240,000-280,000oz) at AISC below US$1,900/oz, and released an updated 10-year production target averaging 533,000oz/year (2026-2035), peaking at 596,000oz in 2030

Council of Ministers of Burkina Faso considered a draft decree on the government's additional equity stake in Kiaka SA; WAF provided a market update on the status of discussions, characterising government engagement as cooperative

ASX trading suspension (imposed late August 2025 pending disclosure) lifted after WAF released a comprehensive statement addressing the Burkina Faso government's request to acquire an additional 35% of Kiaka SA

WAF shares suspended from ASX trading after the Burkina Faso government requested to acquire, for paid consideration, an additional 35% interest in Kiaka SA (on top of its existing 15% free-carried stake), and WAF failed to provide required disclosure within the allotted time
Kiaka transitioned from construction to operations phase (1 August 2025) following completion ahead of schedule and under budget; first gold poured June 2025

Burkina Faso free-carried equity interest in Sanbrado (SOMISA), Kiaka SA and Toega SA increased from 10% to 15% (WAF's interest reduced from 90% to 85%) under alignment with the new 2024 Mining Code; priority dividend to the state (15% of distributable profits) became non-discretionary
Burkina Faso gold royalty rate uncapped - previously capped at 7% when gold price ≥US$2,000/oz, now escalates stepwise up to 12%+ as gold price rises above US$5,000/oz

FY2025 annual results: record group production of 300,383oz (Sanbrado 205,228oz + Kiaka 95,155oz partial year) at AISC US$1,488/oz; net profit A$567.4M, operating cash flow A$789.7M, free cash inflow A$202.6M (positive, first year since Kiaka construction began) and year-end net cash A$145.9M

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 result / 2026 production guidance (March-April 2026) reaffirmed at Q2 2026 update (July 2026)

items.notes: First full year combining Sanbrado (190,000-210,000oz) and Kiaka (240,000-280,000oz); record group output versus 300,383oz in FY2025 (Kiaka only operating for 5 months). On track per Q1 and Q2 2026 production updates despite a Kiaka explosives permit issue.

Reflects Kiaka's higher ramp-up cost profile (H1 2026 AISC US$1,823/oz) and a higher Burkina Faso government royalty burden (uncapped regime, escalating with gold price) partially offsetting Sanbrado's lower-cost profile.

items.target: average 533,000 oz/year (2026-2035), peaking at 596,000oz in 2030; >500,000oz/year continuously 2027-2035
items.notes: Updated 31 March 2026 (ASX announcement 'WAF 10-year gold production to average 533,000 oz per annum'), up from the prior August 2025 target of 480,000oz average (2025-2034, peaking 569,000oz in 2029).
Targeting resource-to-reserve conversion at M1 South, M5 South, Toega underground (maiden underground reserve targeted 2027) and broader Markoyé fault exploration.

items.metric: Kiaka SA equity sale / special dividend
items.notes: Funded by proceeds from the Burkina Faso government's ~CFA70bn (~A$175M) acquisition of an additional 25% of Kiaka SA; record date 18 September 2026. Transaction to complete by year-end 2026, after which WAF's Kiaka SA interest will be 60% (from 85%).

guidance.management_commentary: Executive Chairman and CEO Richard Hyde has emphasised WAF's transition to a +500,000oz per annum, two-mine gold producer, describing 2025 as achieving all five key operational objectives (Kiaka construction and ramp-up, Sanbrado delivery, owner-mining transition, 10-year production profile growth). Management has characterised engagement with the Burkina Faso government over the Kiaka stake increase as cooperative, noting the Government has affirmed commitment to an outcome that 'respects the legitimate interests of all parties, including the financial interests of existing shareholders and lenders,' and has confirmed Sanbrado and Toega are not part of these discussions. Management plans to return the A$175M Kiaka stake-sale proceeds to shareholders via special dividend rather than retain for reinvestment, signalling confidence in organic funding of remaining growth (Toega, M5 South) from operating cash flow.

bull_case: Record gold price environment (US$4,700+/oz realised in H1 2026) combined with WAF's 100% unhedged production is driving record profit, cash flow and a rapidly strengthening balance sheet (A$488M net cash at June 2026, up from a net debt position a year earlier)

Two-mine platform (Sanbrado + Kiaka) now both in production for the first time, with a long-dated (18-20 year Kiaka mine life, 11+ year Sanbrado/Toega life) reserve base and a credible, consistently-updated 10-year production target now averaging 533,000oz/year through 2035

Kiaka ramp-up largely de-risked - construction completed ahead of schedule and under budget, first gold poured June 2025, national grid power connected December 2025, and 2026 guidance reaffirmed through Q2 despite a permitting hiccup

Burkina Faso sovereign risk around Kiaka appears to be resolving on commercially reasonable terms (paid consideration of ~A$175M for the government's additional 25% stake, funded back to shareholders via special dividend) rather than uncompensated expropriation, and explicitly excludes Sanbrado and Toega
Continued exploration success and reserve growth (Ore Reserves up from 4.6Moz in 2022 to 6.5Moz in 2025) extends mine life and underwrites the long-term production target without reliance on M&A
bear_case: 100% single-country asset concentration in Burkina Faso, a military-led government since a 2022 coup facing an active regional jihadist insurgency, exposes WAF to sovereign/political risk that can crystallise rapidly - as shown by the August-November 2025 ASX trading suspension triggered by a government stake demand

Demonstrated pattern of escalating Burkina Faso resource nationalism under the 2024 Mining Code: free-carry stake already raised from 10% to 15% across all subsidiaries in 2025, and a further government move to take Kiaka SA to 40% government ownership (from 15%) shows the state is willing and able to compel additional dilution; a similar demand at Sanbrado or Toega cannot be ruled out

Government gold royalty regime is now uncapped and escalates with gold price (7% to 12%+), meaning WAF captures a shrinking marginal share of further gold price appreciation just as royalties become a larger absolute cost (A$181.5M paid in H1 2026 alone)

Kiaka's all-in sustaining costs during ramp-up (~US$1,700-1,900/oz) are running well above Sanbrado's mature cost base (~US$1,240-1,488/oz), and a 2026 explosives permit issue already curtailed Kiaka open-pit mining - illustrating execution risk remains even post-construction

Heavy reliance on a sustained high gold price to justify current valuation (market cap ~A$4.3B, analyst targets implying material upside) - a material pullback in gold prices would compress margins across both mines simultaneously with no hedging buffer and no geographic diversification to offset it
